meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now, what do you actually have on the essay?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.

I'm writing those times down. A history shows when something was typed, Hale, not how it was written, and he could have drafted it by hand first. Either way, the zero went in before anyone called me, so what is your next step on that?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
Okay. Then the zero stays off while you look, and this stays quiet. Is anything on his record right now?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line? Students misquote from memory all the time, so I want the exact words and the page in front of me. And you haven't answered what I asked about his record.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom and a weekend at a desk are different conditions. But I've read it, and I'm not arguing this one. What are you proposing, because if it's a rewrite, it's private, not in front of his class, and I get in writing that nothing goes on his file?

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. Owen will do the rewrite, to put this behind him. I want the email tonight with all of that in it, and the zero off the gradebook until the rewrite is marked.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite under 4.4, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook until the rewrite is marked, and a straight answer on whether anything is on his record now. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight, the zero off the gradebook until it is marked, and an answer on whether anything is on his record now; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence, then gave dated evidence she could check, and your offer to look at any earlier draft file with its dates answered her one defence.
What cost ground: Nothing cost much, but when she asked for the exact line you said was not in the play, you never gave it, so a strong point went unused and she could not check it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits late on October 28, came close to that night, which is why she went shorter and pushed on procedure, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked which line, give the exact words and the scene at once, so the quotation is on the table before she can raise a doubt.
